#1166. Ancelotti to be inducted into Milan Hall of Fame on Dec 6

Brazil coach Carlo Ancelotti will return to San Siro ahead of the Serie A match against Parma to be inducted into the Milan Hall of Fame on December 6, after he was named one of the three best midfielders in their history.

Milan confirmed that he will be present to receive the special award, designed by Tiffany & Co, from former teammate Daniele Massaro before kick-off.

It is a fitting choice of fixture, as Parma is his hometown club and another of his former teams.

Although many will remember him above all for his record as a coach on the Rossoneri bench, Ancelotti was also a key part of the team that won everything under Arrigo Sacchi.

He wore the Milan jersey from 1987 until his retirement in 1992, making 160 appearances with 11 goals and 12 assists.

With that team, he won two European Cups, two Serie A titles, two UEFA Super Cups, one Intercontinental Cup, and one Italian Super Cup.

Ancelotti returned to San Siro as a coach from 2001 to 2009, winning two Champions League trophies, one Scudetto, two UEFA Super Cups, one Club World Cup, one Coppa Italia and one Italian Super Cup.

#1165. An enduring climatic burden from past peatland drainage

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Over millennia, peatlands have removed hundreds of gigatonnes of carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere but emitted a proportion back as methane (CH4), exerting a slow net cooling effect1. Artificial drainage of these ecosystems—a centuries-old practice2,3—causes decomposition and the re-release of CO2 but suppresses CH4 emissions4, with a net climatic effect that is not well quantified at the global scale5. Here we reconstructed the radiative forcing from worldwide peatland drainage over 1800–2020 by combining a new flux dataset, hydrologically driven models of CO2 and CH4 fluxes and a hindcast of drainage extent and intensity. We found that drainage has produced a net heating effect of +73 (48–99) mW m−2—equivalent to 2.7 (1.8–3.6)% of industrial-era radiative forcing—originating from 0.4–0.5% of global land area. The net heating results from the dominant forcing of drainage-induced CO2 emissions (+83 (52–110) mW m−2) over that of avoided CH4 emissions (−9 (−15–−2) mW m−2). Even without further expansion of drainage, maintaining currently drained areas could almost double the cumulative warming by 2100. Our reconstruction captures the opposing impacts of peatland drainage on global budgets of CO2 and CH4 and quantifies the strong legacy effects of historical drainage on present and possibly future climate.

#1164. Serie A Liveblog: Inter-Genoa, Torino-Lazio and Frosinone-Parma

Join us for all the build-up and action as it happens from today’s three Serie A games: Frosinone-Parma, Torino-Lazio and Inter-Genoa.

We begin at 15:00 CET [14:00 GMT] with Frosinone hosting strugglers Parma at the Stadio Stirpe.

The Ciociari sit in seventh in a European spot, but have lost their last two league matches. Parma, meanwhile, travel to Frosinone after a 5-1 loss to Roma last weekend.

The Ducali, coached by Italy 2006 World Cup winner Alberto Gilardino, have lost three of their last five games, including the last two, and have eight points.

Serie A leaders Lazio visit Torino at 18:00 CET [17:00 GMT] in a reunion between former Milan players Gennaro Gattuso and Ignazio Abate. Gattuso also coached Abate at San Siro.

Lazio are the only unbeaten team in Serie A this season alongside city rivals Roma, but will play Torino without the injured Kenneth Taylor.

Inter-Genoa ends today’s Serie A program at 20:45 CET. The Nerazzurri and the Grifone will meet again next Tuesday, also at San Siro, in the Coppa Italia Round of 16.

Cristian Chivu explains his Inter decisions when hosting Genoa in Serie A this evening, with some changes forced by injuries. ‘We need to be ready for anything.’

“We wish Ostigard all the best, both for a full recovery and his birthday. We thought it was something less serious, but he is back in hospital and will be there for at least a couple more days. It’s best that the doctors discuss this more than me, but we are by his side.”

Click here to read about the latest on the Genoa defender.

If you haven’t checked, then Josep Martinez is not even on the Inter bench. This is due to a knock to the thigh, nothing serious, and he was going to be rested today anyway.

Another touchline reunion, this time between former Roma teammates Cristian Chivu and Daniele De Rossi.

Lazio extended their stay at the top of the table, as Oliver Provstgaard and Gustav Isaksen struck just before half-time for a 2-1 victory away to Torino, despite a Che Adams goal.

Torino attack again, Mandas quick off his line to palm the ball off the head of Oristanio!

Frattesi with a decisive clearance as the free kick bobbles around inside the box!

Another wasted Pinamonti chance, blasting over!

Inter: Provedel; Bisseck, Akanji, Carlos Augusto; Diouf, Barella, Sucic, Jones, Dimarco; Thuram, Lautaro Martinez

Genoa: Bijlow; Marcandalli, Otoa, Vasquez; Ehizibue, Wiafe, Traoré, Mitaj; Ellertsson, Messias; Osmajic

Coco booked for tripping Rovella right on the edge of the area.

Now Torino threaten, Patterson cross nodded just wide by Oristanio!

Pedraza sent through by Frattesi, finish parried by Perri’s leg, then somehow Pinamonti turns the rebound wide!

Patterson is visibly exhausted, but Torino completed all their subs.

Oristanio blasts over, but Duvan Zapata had pulled it out of play anyway.

Cancellieri and Lazzari on for Lazio, Isaksen and Floriani Mussolini off.

Patterson does well to get down the right, but then the cross is wayward and he’s got cramp.

Daniel Braganca and Pellegri on (remember him, folks?), Adams and Mandragora off.

Pellegri’s first game since December 2025.

Cacciamani hobbles off the field, replaced by Fortini.

Hmm, Cacciamani just pulled up clutching the back of his left thigh. That’s not good.

Dele-Bashiru surge forward, pass for Gudmundsson, but the shot is charged down.

Pinamonti and Gudmundsson on for the first Lazio changes, replacing Zaccagni and Noslin.

Che Adams gives Torino a lifeline 👀🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿

It’s 2-1 in Turin and the Granata are right back in this contest 🐂

#1163. Brighton underline title credentials with impressive win over Man City

This Brighton and Hove Albion title challenge – as it must now be classed – flies in the face of the saying that money always talks in football. Manchester City have been found guilty of breaching financial rules and also fielded the most expensive midfield in Premier League history here, yet the match-winners cost a fraction in comparison.

Looking at Brighton’s winning goal, it was created by a cross that flashed across the City goal from Diego Gómez, an £11m signing who was playing in Major League Soccer in the United States not so long ago. Maxim de Cuyper, a £17.5m arrival from Club Brugge, was credited with the assist after Yasin Ayari tapped in.

Ayari cost £3.5m from Swedish club AIK and scored in the 5-0 wins over Coventry and Palace, and now has this winner to add to his collection. The 23-year-old is another example of Brighton polishing these gems and putting them together in a team that can win against any opponent in the Premier League.

It could keep them at the top end of the table for a good while longer. They have already shown they can defeat Arsenal in a one-off match and they look to have the ingredients to stay the pace with them. In Fabian Hürzeler they have one of the brightest young coaches in the Premier League and he has a squad that are all on the same page.

Leicester upset the odds 10 years ago with a settled team, while this Brighton team has a deeper squad. When the substitutes came on in the second half, they slotted into a well-rehearsed system.

“We faced adversity. There was a little bit of luck but in the end they deserved it because they worked hard for it,” said Hürzeler. “I want players who want to compete, to dominate. They all have the winning mentality inside of them. These kinds of performances are not about one or two players, everyone has to stick together.”

LOVE THIS TEAM SO MUCH! 🤩 https://t.co/QdBXsW1Ze5

Hürzeler has played down a title challenge but his team have been among the most impressive in the first part of the season. The German coach, 33, has been in English football for two years but has learnt quickly the tried-and-tested response of taking each game as it comes. Next is Getafe in the Europa Conference League on Thursday.

While Hürzeler was reluctant to name individual performers, Dutch goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen was another key player in this win. He kept out Iliman Ndiaye and repelled Erling Haaland, who lost a physical battle with Lewis Dunk. “You’re going down with the Palace,” chanted the jubilant Brighton fans, with City now losing two Premier League games in a row.

City head coach Enzo Maresca will be content with the number of chances his team created but there must be concerns at the other end. He tried a change of formula, dropping Marc Guéhi to the bench for the first time this season, yet his team were still prone to individual errors.

“We are the second team in scoring in the Premier League. We are scoring goals but in this moment we are conceding silly goals. We can avoid that,” Maresca said. His team have conceded 10 goals in their last six games, which is not the foundation of a title challenge, even if City have been stacking up points.

Maresca picked a midfield that cost £327m to recruit this summer, with Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernández and Ayyoub Bouaddi picked together for the first time. There were some signs they could all play together, although City looked more dangerous when Rayan Cherki came off the bench to break up the trio.

Pascal Gross cost a nominal fee when he returned to Brighton but his hard work and intelligent passing means Brighton can control periods of the game even against the very best.

The goal came when Brighton switched play from a free-kick, although City thought Anderson was victim rather than perpetrator. Former Inter Miami winger Gómez provided the cross that opened up City, with Gianluigi Donnarumma guilty of not coming out to claim the ball, then Matheus Nunes slipped at the vital moment.

“Unfortunately it is happening for our players but I think it is part of the game, part of football, it happens many times against us, we need to analyse and understand what we can do better,” Maresca added. City also felt Dunk used his arm to block the ball in the penalty area, although no spot-kick was given.

It was a sweet goal by Ayari, who had missed a penalty in the shoot-out last week when the teams played in the EFL Cup. Brighton stayed in Manchester after the defeat, masterminding a win that means they have now defeated all of the traditional heavyweight teams in the Premier League.

“I wasn’t aware of that. For me it’s more important, not about history, it’s about giving something back to the supporters. They’ve spent a lot of time and money,” Hürzeler said.

“We’ll take it game by game. See what happens because we have loads of games. Just focussing every day on what’s ahead of us and the job we have. We will continue to do that and see where it leaves us at the end of the season. We are happy with the way we are playing - not just the results but the way we are playing too. We have to continue to develop that style and ruthlessness and we can do great things.”

League leaders defeated ✅ @BHAFC are closing in on top spot 👏 https://t.co/j0Dbqr12Vv

Important to note they’ve also scored 16 goals in the process without reply.

SIX wins in a row 👏👏👏👏👏👏 https://t.co/8S0DpVTzAD

Bournemouth 2 Leeds 0 (Adli) Kroupi threads a phenomenal pass through Ampadu’s legs to the onrushing Adli, who rounds off the win with a delightful finish.

Brighton have done it. Their impressive season continues as Hurzeler’s side condemn Man City to back-to-back Premier League defeats. This result also means that Brighton close the gap on the hosts at the top of the table to just two points. They’ve avenged that midweek League Cup loss in style.

THREE HUGE POINTS FOR THE ALBION! 😍 https://t.co/jQ7GwCKbT2

We’re halfway through four minutes of added time. Can Brighton hold on for a statement victory?

O’Reilly misses a sitter. Verbruggen blocks Khusanov’s effort and the rebound falls to O’Reilly who somehow directs it wide from a few yards out. He has to score that. It was agonisingly close to a late Man City leveller.

Brighton are so close to a second, which would have settled this tie. Rutter spearheads a counter attack and cleverly plays in Hinshelwood, who is one-on-one with Donnarumma and attempts an ambitious chip over the goalkeeper. However, his effort drifts into the side netting. Nearly game, set and match for the visitors.

Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al-Mubarak is here at the Etihad Stadium, sat next to CEO Ferran Soriano.

City’s chances have fallen to Iliman Ndiaye, rather than Erling Haaland. Haaland has been preoccupied with battling Lewis Dunk. Enzo Maresca surely won’t be too concerned if this stays 0-1 - his team have created lots of attacks. But their defence is a problem, with 10 goals conceded in the last six games.

Still, Brighton are holding firm against Man City. Foden and Allan have entered the action, with Ndiaye and Gvardiol withdrawn. Brighton have made five changes since the 64th minute, with Hadjam, Wieffer, Hinshelwood, Yalcouye and Rutter all on from the bench.

Hull City 2 Ipswich 2 (Enciso) The playmaker bags a stunner as he whips an exquisite effort from outside the box into the net. Enciso has now scored in back-to-back league matches.

How have Man City not scored?! O’Reilly darts into the box and squares the ball for Ndiaye, who knocks his close-range effort wide.

Brentford 2 Forest 0 (Igor Thiago) Forest’s wastefulness in front of goal has been punished, with Igor Thiago adding a second for Brentford.

Hull City 2 Ipswich 1 (McBurnie) Two goals in quick succession for the hosts. McBurnie sneaks a low free-kick into the net. Despite Walton’s best efforts, he couldn’t keep it out. No one could have envisioned this on the basis of Hull’s poor first half display.

It’s wave after wave of Man City pressure. O’Reilly also recently replaced Fernandez as Maresca continues to plot a route back into this contest.

Coventry 3 Sunderland 1 (Le Fee) The visitors are awarded a penalty after Pinnock is deemed to have handled O’Nein’s goalbound effort. Le Fee steps up and converts. Is the comeback on?

Cherki and Nunes link up, with the latter driving into the box. He cuts inside and shoots, but his fierce effort is superbly saved by Verbruggen. Haaland can’t quite latch onto the rebound. Cherki is starting to pull the strings for the hosts.

This game could go either way. City have been bright, with Ndiaye hitting the crossbar and Mateus Nunes forcing an excellent save from Bart Verbruggen. But Brighton are not parking the bus and are also bringing on fresh legs. Mats Wieffer and Jaouen Hadjam are on and have slotted into the gameplan.

Hull 1 Ipswich 1 (Iroegbunam) The Hull midfielder has his first Premier League goal as no one in an Ipswich shirt puts any pressure on Iroegbunam, allowing him to advance incredibly far forward into the penalty area before smashing into the net.

Get in, Tim 😮‍💨💪 🐯 1-1 🚜 [64'] https://t.co/Amq0yxbgr0

Coventry 3 Sunderland 0 (Rudoni) Things go from bad to worse for Sunderland... Coventry are in dreamland. It’s a horrible goal for Sunderland to concede. Rudoni’s long-range strike deflects off Alderete’s outstretched leg and flies past Roefs into the net.

Brighton threaten at the start of the second half as Ayari attempts to run provider, squaring a perfectly-weighted ball across to De Cuyper, who wastefully directs it off target. Man City are very lucky to remain just one goal behind.

Bournemouth 1 Leeds 0 (Evanilson) Against the run of play, Bournemouth have the lead and it’s a terrible mistake from Trafford, who was excellent at Sunderland last weekend. #1162. Alvini ‘certainly pleasing’ to hear Frosinone praise and see Mancini in the stands

Massimiliano Alvini admits it is ‘certainly pleasing’ that Frosinone are discussed by Como’s Cesc Fabregas and Francesco Farioli of FC Porto, while Italy coach Roberto Mancini was in the stands to watch them today.

The Canarini are one of the big surprises of the Serie A season so far, having earned promotion from Serie B as runners-up to Venezia last year.

They sparked a public debate after the 5-1 defeat to Milan at San Siro, earning praise from the likes of Fabregas and Farioli for sticking to their ideas, even if it left them open to being ripped apart by counter-attacks.

Frosinone got back on track today with a 3-0 victory over Parma, their sixth in a row on home turf, thanks to the Tomas Bobcek hat-trick.

“It is certainly pleasing that Fabregas and Farioli are talking about Frosinone, and it means a lot for us, but we still need to keep working,” said Alvini in his press conference.

“What matters to me is playing good football, and we saw a good Frosinone in these first 13 rounds, including the defeat to Milan.”

There was another sign of how far Frosinone have come this season by the fact Italy coach Mancini was in the stands.

It came after some controversy in the media over the fact midfielder Giacomo Calò was snubbed for the recent Nations League squad.

“I am glad that Mancini came, I’m happy for Frosinone, and hope that he saw an enjoyable game of football,” added Alvini.

“Anyone who knows me can tell you Mancini was one of my favourite football players, so it’s a personal satisfaction that he came to see us.”

Frosinone notably also play more Italians than any other team in Serie A, although top scorer Antonio Raimondo was only fit for the bench this afternoon.

They have amassed seven wins, two draws and four defeats in Serie A so far this season, scoring 28 goals and conceding 20.

#1161. Xabi Alonso tells angry Chelsea fans to back Wesley Fofana after they told him to 'f*** off' during desperate defeat by Nottingham Forest

Published: 18:09 EST, 27 November 2026 | Updated: 18:33 EST, 27 November 2026

Xabi Alonso called on Chelsea’s fans to support Wesley Fofana after their away end spent their latest defeat chanting for their own player to get out of their club.

Fofana started against Nottingham Forest after apologising for the unauthorised interview he had conducted with a French YouTube channel. The content of that chat included him laughing off how he missed the penalty which condemned Chelsea to their Carabao Cup exit at Liverpool.

From the first minute at the City Ground, he was booed on the ball and subjected to abusive singing from Chelsea’s supporters, who chanted: ‘F*** off Fofana, you’re not wanted here.’

Fofana went on to give away a penalty by fouling his former team-mate Liam Delap and was then replaced by Levi Colwill, who had been dropped from the line-up instead of the Frenchman.

From the first minute at the City Ground, Fofana was booed on the ball and subjected to abusive singing from Chelsea’s fans, who chanted: ‘F*** off Fofana, you’re not wanted here'

Alonso confirmed he had not yet spoken with Fofana after full-time and added at his post-match press conference on the fans: ‘We need to support everyone because we need everyone. We need the fans, we need the players, we need to stick together because if not, things will get more complicated. We need to help. We need to go through this together.’

Alonso also would not confirm if he will leave Fofana out of Chelsea’s next game at home to Crystal Palace on Wednesday despite what turned into an ugly night here for his team.

‘We are going through a difficult moment of confidence, things are not clicking, not going the way we want,’ Alonso added. ‘We know in football, this can change quickly or can continue. It's down to us to work to find those solutions to have a better feeling on the pitch and to get better results because that's what we need.

Forest manager Oliver Glasner added: ‘We were struggling at the beginning to score the goals, especially here at the City Ground. We could see the progress but we couldn't get the results in many other games and now it's of course to keep working. Just 12 games played with 12 points so it's still not satisfying for us. Many games to go and for us it's to stay humble and keep working.’

#1160. Vanoli: ‘I am the right man in the right place’ to rescue Fiorentina

Paolo Vanoli believes he is ‘the right man in the right place’ to rescue Fiorentina all over again, as they prepare for a relegation battle with Udinese.

It kicks off at the Bluenergy Arena on Sunday at 11.30 GMT (12.30 CET).

These are two big clubs who are regulars in the top flight, yet it is a relegation tussle because Udinese are rock bottom on six points, and the Viola not too far above them on nine.

“The lads need to play in a courageous way, aware of their position in the table, and of the errors that have been made in important games,” said Vanoli in his press conference.

“This is what I told them, and what I mean, seeing as there was controversy last time I urged humility. In my view, humility means being fully aware of your situation.”

Fiorentina were hammered 3-0 by Monza on Monday evening, a rude awakening after a three-match unbeaten run.

Vanoli rescued the team from relegation last season, was released to make way for Fabio Grosso, then brought back again just a few weeks into the campaign.

“Any coach in this line of work knows he is never safe or comfortable. What interests me is Fiorentina, not my job. I am thinking about what is best for the team. There’s no point looking back over our shoulders,” said the coach.

Fiorentina start every season with high hopes, yet seem to be going backwards each season, battling against the threat of relegation.

“I believe the project is one aimed to dream, but it takes time and there is a process,” added Vanoli.

“Why should I step aside? I remain convinced that I am the right man in the right place.”

#1159. Cruel Xabi Alonso threw poor Wesley Fofana to the lions by starting him: Chelsea boss was as much at fault as his liability of a defender - and he is risking losing the fans with his baffling decisions, writes KIERAN GILL

Published: 02:00 EST, 28 November 2026 | Updated: 06:21 EST, 28 November 2026

We know what Chelsea’s fans thought of Wesley Fofana starting. Whenever he had the ball, boos spilled out of the away end, and a few times, there was one song filling the City Ground.

‘F*** off Fofana, you’re not wanted here,’ it went. It started from the first minute, but was at its loudest when he bundled over Liam Delap for Nottingham Forest's penalty for 2-0 and then when he was put out of his misery after 56 minutes, substituted for Levi Colwill.

As much as it was on Fofana – after that unauthorised interview in which he laughed off his penalty miss which confirmed their Carabao Cup exit to Liverpool, showing nowhere near the winning mentality these fans expect within their club – it was also on his manager Xabi Alonso.

It was the easy decision to drop Fofana. It was there, staring at Alonso. Poor performances have become the norm from the 25-year-old Frenchman this season. Against Leeds. Against Liverpool. Against Manchester United. Chelsea’s £75million defender was a liability against them all.

Then he handed his manager another reason to leave him out of his starting line-up with that interview conducted behind his club’s back. Fofana made a few faux pas in it, not least by mentioning how he was advised that he still had so much money to make out of his £200,000-per-week contract when he considered quitting football. But had Alonso listened to it, he would have also heard how Fofana’s mental health suffered while he was trying to battle back from his injury hell.

Xabi Alonso's decision to start Wesley Fofana was cruel - and the defender returned a mistake-addled performance

Fofana fouled Liam Delap to give away a penalty on another night of chaos for Chelsea

Yet Chelsea’s manager exposed him here. Cruelly, we could even say, after what turned into an excruciating experience for Fofana. Alonso must have known he might be subjected to such abuse. It was surely flagged by someone inside of the club as a risk.

Alonso cannot blame starting Fofana on having no other options at centre back. The very fact he used Moises Caicedo in central defence in the place of Colwill showed it could be done. That was a problem in itself, taking Chelsea’s best midfielder out of where they needed him most.

And so, Fofana started, struggled, heard the abuse, made a mess of one long ball and then tripped Delap. With that, Chelsea were two goals down, and on their way to a fourth defeat in five league games. Alonso was noncommittal when asked how on earth he could use Fofana again after this, but it is hard to see how he can start when Crystal Palace visit Stamford Bridge on Wednesday.

Alonso has now overseen the same number of Premier League losses as the sacked Liam Rosenior – six – but in fewer games managed – 12 to his predecessor’s 13.

Chelsea’s manager is making problems for himself amid it all. By starting Fofana. By selecting Danny Welbeck over Emmanuel Emegha. By not bringing on Estevao when the away end were singing the substitute’s name while Chelsea were already trailing by two goals.

Alonso was wrong to start Danny Welbeck and wrong to put Moises Caicedo at centre-back

Alonso’s decisions and his declining to explain them afterwards brought to mind that scene from Moneyball. The one where Billy Beane (played by Brad Pitt) is telling Peter Brand (Jonah Hill): ‘It's a problem that you think we need to explain ourselves. Don't. To anyone.’

Yet sometimes, an explanation would help. Alonso was asked at his post-match press conference to tell us his tactical thinking behind Fofana over Colwill. He did not, instead saying: ‘It's always the best tactical decisions approaching each game and today that was my decision.’

It is not the first time he has been unwilling or unable to articulate the reasoning behind one of his bold calls, and that is an issue for the fans who are quickly losing their faith.

After full-time, Alonso stood in front of the away end at the City Ground and stared, presumably to take his medicine after orchestrating this latest Premier League loss.

Imagine you are Delap, Igor Jesus or Morgan Gibbs-White. You see Chelsea have named their centre backs as Fofana and Caicedo. You are happy with that.

Then imagine you are James McAtee or Xaver Schlager. You see Chelsea have taken Caicedo out of their midfield and added in Jordan Henderson next to Romeo Lavia. You are happy with that.

Then imagine you are Jair Cunha, Nikola Milenkovic or Murillo. You see Chelsea have selected Welbeck, 36, rather than the unpredictable and enthusiastic Emegha, 23. You are happy with that.

Emmanuel Emegha was a bright spot for Chelsea, coming off the bench to score twice

Forest's players can only have fancied their chances from the moment they saw what the opposition was putting up, and Alonso’s selections facilitated that optimism. The fact that Welbeck was hooked at half-time told us he knew he got it wrong. Emegha was introduced and scored twice, becoming the first substitute to be involved in a goal for Chelsea this season and adding to the goal he scored in their 4-1 loss to Leeds from last weekend.

It was Emegha who gave his side a fighting chance while Cole Palmer put in yet another anonymous performance and with Morgan Rogers joining him on this occasion.

Tactically, Alonso cannot hide from these bad showings. We see clearer patterns in Jackson Pollock paintings. Chelsea tried three different set-piece routines from the training ground here, as if they needed an alternative way to try to get a goal because they have been so unthreatening from open play of late. None of Austin MacPhee’s wacky ideas worked here.

But Palmer is letting his club down especially, having only signed his new contract until 2034 last month. Perhaps he is now too comfortable with that tidy bump.

#1158. Serie A official line-ups: Inter vs. Genoa

Lautaro Martinez returns to the starting XI after six weeks out with Curtis Jones, but Inter miss Alessandro Bastoni and Hakan Calhanoglu against on-form Genoa and Milutin Osmajic.

It kicks off at San Siro at 19.45 GMT (20.45 CET).

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from today’s three Serie A games on the Liveblog.

The Nerazzurri have had a mixed week, as they fumbled a 4-2 lead for a dramatic 4-4 Serie A draw against Atalanta, then registered a third straight Champions League win by beating VfB Stuttgart 2-0.

Lautaro Martinez came off the bench and scored in that midweek match, and here he gets his first start since that thigh injury on October 10.

Marcus Thuram partners him upfront, sending Pio Esposito to the bench after a remarkable run of games, including a hat-trick against Atalanta.

Bastoni limped off with a muscular problem against Stuttgart, so joins Calhanoglu and Ange-Yoan Bonny on the treatment table.

Ivan Provedel is given a rare opportunity in goal to rest Josep Martinez, who has a slight thigh issue.

Curtis Jones gets a chance to prove himself in midfield during Calhanoglu’s absence.

Genoa have really turned a corner in recent weeks, winning four of their last five games, interrupted only by a hard-fought 2-1 home defeat to Milan.

The star has been without doubt Osmajic, as the former Preston North End striker has six goals in 11 Serie A games, including a brace in last week’s victory away to Sassuolo.

However, Leo Ostigard is spending his birthday in hospital after suffering from a high fever and strong headaches over the last few days.

The defender had been released on Wednesday, only to be brought back in for observation today.

This isn’t the only issue, as Genoa will be without Lorenzo Colombo for the rest of the season with a torn anterior cruciate ligament, while Tommaso Baldanzi is also dealing with a calf issue.

Sebastian Otoa therefore steps into the back three, with Mikael Ellertsson and Junior Messias supporting Osmajic.

Curiously, these two teams will meet again on Tuesday evening in the Coppa Italia Round of 16.

#1157. Spurs win three in row for first time in 616 days to pile pressure on Sage

For the first time in 616 days, Tottenham Hotspur have won three Premier League matches in a row. Three different managers have been sacked in that time, and the mood in north London had plunged to grim lows, but finally there is a sense that something truly exciting is stirring at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

This victory over Crystal Palace was not as impressive as last week’s triumph at Chelsea, but it did not need to be. After Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta was sent off in the 13th minute, Spurs simply had to make their numerical advantage count. They did so with relative ease, taking complete control of possession and creating endless goalscoring opportunities.

Roberto De Zerbi’s team ended the night with 34 shots to Palace’s two and with 758 completed passes to Palace’s 149. The goals ultimately came from two defenders, Archie Gray and Jan Paul van Hecke, but there was a long list of Spurs players who might have scored here.

Spurs take the lead through an Archie Gray header! ⚪ https://t.co/qSCECkOJur

Did this defeat mark the end for Pierre Sage, the Palace manager? The Frenchman was only appointed in June but it has been a grisly start to the campaign. Palace have the worst defence in the league, have lost six of nine games and have not produced any truly encouraging performances in the Premier League.

Even in the two games Palace have won, against Fulham and Nottingham Forest, they were lucky to do so. The likes of Sean Dyche and Thomas Frank, both of whom would be strong candidates to replace Sage if Palace do pull the trigger, will no doubt have been keeping an eye on events here.

“I am really aware of the situation,” Sage said. “I don’t like this situation. [But] you can trust in me, I will never give up. I want to be the first on the pitch on Monday. I have the rage to train more. It’s not me to decide this thing [his future]. If I have one hour, I will give my best for one hour. If I have 10 years, I will give my best for 10 years.”

The decision for Palace chairman Steve Parish, then, is whether this result represented a continuation of the team’s problems or was an aberration caused by the early red card. It would be reasonable for Sage to claim this match was out of his hands from the moment Mateta lunged at Spurs captain Micky van de Ven, but such an argument might not carry much weight with Palace sitting 18th in the table.

The challenge was foolish in the extreme by Mateta, a player who was much more successful in exiting this game than he has been in his numerous attempts to leave Palace in recent transfer windows. At first glance it did not seem the worst tackle, but the replays were damning: Mateta led with his studs and made forceful contact with Van de Ven’s ankle.

It was an inexcusably brainless act, after just 13 minutes of play, and the same could be said of Palace’s defending from a right-wing corner a few minutes later. Mohammed Kudus swirled the delivery to the back post, where Gray was unmarked. Yes, Palace were defending with 10. But no, that does not justify the inability of Sage’s players to spot Gray. Even more embarrassingly, the Tottenham player was unmarked again from another corner shortly afterwards.

It was not the first time this season that Palace’s cause has been undermined by a red card. When they lost at home to Ipswich Town in September, Axel Disasi was sent off after 34 minutes. An absence of discipline? Perhaps. Sage might argue, though, that he is not responsible for his players demonstrating a lack of basic brainpower.

Jean-Philippe Mateta receives his first red card for Crystal Palace! 🟥 https://t.co/U9UYb29mbk

All of this was welcomed heartily by the Spurs fans, who celebrated Mateta’s dismissal as though it was a goal. Recent results have restored some of the enthusiasm in this corner of north London and the mood here was buoyant, even before Gray’s opener.

“Now we are playing as a team,” De Zerbi said. “Before the international break, we were playing as many good players but not as a team. We showed our maturity. We are improving.”

The second goal was always coming and it arrived in the 73rd minute, when Van Hecke attacked a wonderful cross by Mateus Fernandes. Palace goalkeeper Dean Henderson saved the first attempt but the ball dropped onto the head of Van Hecke, now seated in the six-yard box, and he happily nodded it home.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League encounter between Tottenham and Crystal Palace.

Last weekend, Spurs enjoyed a historic result, beating Chelsea 2-0 at Stamford Bridge for only the second time in the league for 36 years thanks to Mike Penders’ own goal and Mathys Tel’s stunning solo strike. This result, coupled with the 3-1 victory over Coventry City in their previous home outing, means that Tottenham have won back-to-back league games and are beginning to gather some momentum under Roberto De Zerbi.

In his pre-match press conference, when asked if he’s felt a change in atmosphere after the triumph at Stamford Bridge, De Zerbi replied: “We have not achieved our goal. We want our fans to be happy, not now, at the end of the season. Now we have to push, we have to stay focused, we have to increase the spirit, the appetite to win games in a row. To do that, we have to show if we are good enough. If we are good enough on the pitch, for sure we are ready. In the head, in the mentality, we have to show, because the step of this club is to win games in a row and to be angry day by day, game by game, win by win. One time or two times are not enough.”

Palace have endured a tricky and inconsistent start to the season under their summer appointment Pierre Sage, accumulating just seven points from their opening seven league matches while shipping 17 goals. The 1-0 League Cup victory over Fulham in midweek has momentarily eased the pressure on the Frenchman, but given their newfound success in recent campaigns, fan expectations have risen, with recent performances prompting some cause for concern.

Tottenham remain without the suspended Rodrigo Bentancur, while Xavi Simons, Wilson Odobert, Lucas Bergvall, Savio, Tosin Adarabioyo and Mykhaylo Mudryk are out injured. James Maddison was substituted early in the second half at Chelsea with an apparent groin strain, but De Zerbi insists he’s available for this one. Destiny Udogie could also be involved after recovering from a knee issue.

The visitors are without the injured trio of Ismaila Sarr, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chadi Riad, but there’s hope that Quinten Timber and Jorgen Strand Larsen are fit to be involved this evening after they both missed the Fulham victory.

Kick-off is at 17:30, with teams coming shortly.

#1156. Ten-man Tenerife beat Badajoz 5-2 in Copa del Rey tie postponed after De Miguel’s death

Tenerife won 5-2 at Badajoz in the Copa del Rey despite finishing the match with ten men. The victory keeps their cup run alive ahead of the second-round draw.

At the Estadio Nuevo Vivero on Wednesday 18 November, Álvaro Cervera’s side booked a place in the second round of the Copa del Rey. The tie had been postponed twice, first after the train accident in Toledo province and then after the death of Tenerife forward Jesús de Miguel on 3 November, who was remembered with a minute’s silence.

Cervera started a line-up made up largely of reserves. It still produced a scoreline Tenerife had never recorded in 260 Copa del Rey matches, according to elDiario.es (Canarias Ahora). About 3,000 spectators watched, around 20 per cent of the stadium’s capacity.

Grant-Leon Ranos opened the scoring in the sixth minute from a Marc Mateu assist. Juanjo Sánchez added a second a minute later. Ranos struck again in the 38th minute, set up by Gerard Valentín.

Carlos Beitia pulled one back for Badajoz in the 49th minute. Roko Jureškin was then sent off in the 58th minute. Ten-man Tenerife still extended the lead through substitute Iván Chapela in the 69th minute, assisted by Martin Pečar.

Jorge Barba replied for the hosts in the 74th minute from a Manuel Hernández assist. Víctor Moreno completed the scoring deep into stoppage time, with Álvarez providing the pass.

The Segunda Federación side went into the tie third in their group. They were also unbeaten in seven league matches in a row.

Tenerife have now come through their opening Copa del Rey tie in eight seasons in a row. The win followed a 2-0 victory over AD Ceuta FC. Before that came a run of draws against FC Andorra, Sabadell, Celta de Vigo II and Girona.

This was the first meeting between the clubs in the cup. They had played each other 22 times in Segunda División. Tenerife won ten of those games, Badajoz eight, and four ended level. Tenerife’s previous visit to Badajoz, on 30 March 2003, ended in a 2-1 defeat under David Amaral.

Cervera’s side return to league duty at home to Mallorca in Segunda División on Saturday 21 November. Badajoz travel to Recreativo Huelva in Segunda División RFEF Group 4 on Sunday 22 November.

The second round will feature 56 teams in 28 one-off ties. The lower-division side hosts if its ground meets federation standards. The draw was put back because of the postponed first-round matches. The Ciudad del Fútbol in Las Rozas, Madrid, home of the federation, is the venue for it.

#1155. Serie A | Torino 1-2 Lazio: Aquile refuse to stop flying

Lazio extended their stay at the top of the table, as Oliver Provstgaard and Gustav Isaksen struck just before half-time for a 2-1 victory away to Torino, despite a Che Adams goal.

Gennaro Gattuso’s men were still unbeaten and top of the Serie A table going into this weekend, but while Mattia Zaccagni returned to the squad after a month out, they lost Kenneth Taylor to injury, joining Nuno Tavares, Josip Sutalo and Adam Marusic on the treatment table. Toro had been in dire form with one point from the last four rounds. Rafik Belghali, Ardian Ismajli and Franco Israel were out injured. It was a touching reunion for former Milan teammates Gennaro Gattuso and Ignazio Abate.

The Granata should’ve taken the lead after six minutes when Danilho Doekhi slowed down Cesare Casadei on the dinked Che Adams pass off the outside of the boot, it fell kindly for Giovanni Simeone, forcing a fantastic one-handed Christos Mandas save.

Mandas also got down to parry a Nikola Vlasic angled drive, while Oliver Provstgaard did just enough to stop Pietro Comuzzo going clear on another inspired Adams pass.

Lazio had a huge chance on 32 minutes when Davide Frattesi rose to meet the Alfonso Pedraza corner, denied by a desperate Lucas Perri one-handed save at the near post.

The deadlock was finally broken from a set play, as Zaccagni’s corner was whipped in for Oliver Provstgaard to shake off Saul Coco and nod into the far bottom corner from eight yards.

Both the Lazio chances had come from set plays, but the second goal was from open play barely 90 seconds later. Zaccagni was involved again, winning it back in the centre-circle and immediately sliding through for Isaksen, who controlled with his weaker right foot, surged forward and bent it into the far bottom corner with the inside of the left boot.

There was almost a third moments later, as Isaksen’s back-heel flick set up Frattesi for an effort that was charged down by Coco.

Torino also threatened, Cesare Casadei turning a free header wide of the back post on a corner on the stroke of half-time.

Simeone had a great opportunity to get his team back into it, but Mandas got down to fingertip the effort onto the base of the upright, then Adams drilled wide as the move continued.

It was only a warning, as Adams glanced his header into the far bottom corner at the near post on the Gvidas Gineitis corner kick to put Torino back in the game.

Adams also had penalty appeals for a Danilho Doekhi challenge, but Frattesi got the ball anyway, and Toro lost Alessio Cacciamani to a left hamstring strain.

Pietro Pellegri came off the bench for his first appearance in almost a year, but Lazio wasted a double opportunity late on. First Perri stuck out a boot to deny Alfonso Pedraza when sent through by Frattesi, then Andrea Pinamonti somehow turned the rebound wide.

Moments later, Torino threatened too, Gaetano Oristanio nodding the Nathan Patterson cross inches past the near post. Lazio were hanging on in added time, Mandas quick off his line to palm the cross off the head of Oristanio.

Provstgaard 42 (L), Isaksen 44 (L), Adams 62 (T)

#1154. Just eight universities dominate Nobel and other top economics prizes

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Sarah Wild is a freelance journalist in Canterbury, UK.

Researchers from Harvard and seven other US universities including MIT, Princeton and Yale, dominate economics prizes.Credit: Jade Gao/AFP via Getty

Major prizes in economics, including the Nobel are being awarded to researchers affiliated to an increasingly concentrated set of US universities, according to a working paper published last month1.

Eight institutions dominate the world's top economics prizes, led Harvard University in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

This contrasts with prizes awarded in disciplines in the natural sciences, engineering and social sciences outside economics. These have become less concentrated among certain instituions over the past 70 years, according to the working paper, which has not yet been peer reviewed.

“The whole world now does science,” says Richard Freeman, an economist at Harvard University and an author on the paper, which is an update to an article presented at a National Bureau of Economic Research Summer Institute workshop in a 20242. “Our initial thought was that as the science spreads out, so too should all the prizes.” And that was the case — except in economics where “it went the other direction”.

Economist John Hassler, who is based at Stockholm University and chairs the prize-awarding committee for the Economics Prize in Memory of Alfred Nobel, says that the overall finding of concentration among a small group of US universities is not a complete surprise.

“The trend is truly eye-opening and adds another dimension to the understanding of inequality within the economics profession,” adds Ashwini Deshpande, an economist at Ashoka University in Sonipat, India. “The low levels of gender, ethnic and geographic diversity within authors of top journal papers and prizes is well known and a matter of concern.”

Freeman and his colleagues examined 171 different awards and focused their analyses on those given between 1960 and 2022, including Nobel prizes (except for literature and peace), the Fields Medal for mathematics and the Breakthrough science prizes established in 2012 by the founders of technology companies among others.

The authors of the working paper analysed the academic affiliations of the 5,859 prizewinners, working out the number of years they were linked to a specific institution. They call this metric ‘affiliation years’.

Of the 18 scientific fields of the prizewinners, 17 had a greater variety of universities represented among recipients over the time period. Economics was the outlier.

Among winners of the economics Nobel prize, seven out of 148 institutions made up 50% of affiliation years. It means that, of all the years that economics Nobel prizewinners dedicated to their discipline in academia, half of them were spent in the seven institutions.

For chemistry Nobels, 23 institutions out of 216 accounted for half of affiliation years. Twenty-six out of 243 institutions accounted for 50% of affiliation years for the physiology or medicine Nobel, and 17 out of 200 for the physics prize.

When the authors assessed all the main economics prizes between 1960 and 2022 (not only the Nobel), they found that researchers from eight out of 249 institutions represented 50% of affiliation years. In addition to Harvard, the eight are: the University of Chicago in Illinois; Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) in Cambridge; Stanford University in California; Princeton University in New Jersey; Yale University in New Haven, Connecticut; the University of California, Berkeley; and Columbia University in New York.

By contrast, for assessed prizes in the natural sciences, 37 institutions out of 1,318 account for 50% of affiliation-years as of 2022; for engineering prizes it is 27 out of 783; and for social sciences prizes (minus economics), it is 23 out of 744. Unlike in economics, the trend for these fields is towards less concentration (see ‘Spot the outlier’).

The authors propose some possible explanations. One of these relates to another finding of the paper: “The institutions producing most of the field’s recognized work also establish the toolkit that the rest of the fields adopts,” the paper’s authors say. “Work using an unfamiliar approach is hard to place or recognize, and findings that disagree with the main tenets of the field are rejected rather than studied as special cases that may yield new knowledge.”

Another factor, they report is that in economics, 55 per cent of Nobel laureates received the prize for a broad body of work. This contrasts somewhat with medicine and the other sciences. Some 50 per cent of prize winners in chemistry, 59 per cent in physics and 70 per cent in medicine were awarded for testable findings.

Hanzhang Zhou, a co-author on the paper and an economics doctoral candidate at MIT, says: “When you’re giving the prize for somebody’s lifetime agenda, the institution that they’re associated with is usually one of the factors that you do take into account,” she explains.

Hassler told Nature that the economics prize is not intended to be a lifetime achievement award and follows the rules governing the other prize categories. He says it is a prize for a well-defined contribution or breakthrough, should also lead to further research in the field and that the finding must also have relevance to society at large.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03333-3

Freeman, R. B., Xie, D., Zhang, H. & Zhou, H. NBER Working Paper 35875 (National Bureau of Economic Research, 2026).

Freeman, R. B., Xie, D., Zhang, H. & Zhou, H. in NBER Summer Institute – The Science of Science Funding https://conference.nber.org/conf_papers/f204525.pdf (2024).

#1153. The Premier League's great shinpad scourge: How rise in footballers using 'sim card' size guards has left fans fuming and youngsters at risk of serious injury

Published: 07:00 EST, 28 November 2026 | Updated: 07:00 EST, 28 November 2026

Is it woke nonsense that footballers wear shin pads with the size and protective capacity of a custard cream?

Forget VAR, forget half-and-half scarfs, forget thirsty Gianni Infantino's drinks breaks, forget teenage tacticos lecturing you about 'pausa' on TikTok - the great shin pad debate has struck 'The Game's Gone' chord and divided fans.

Recent footage of Newcastle's Matias Fernandez-Pardo pulling down his socks to reveal a thin pink foam disk, caused a stir.

'It's a sim card! It's a sanitary product! He's on £100,000-a-week, the club shouldn't pay him if he snaps his leg in half! - The complaints poured in but Fernandez-Pardo is not alone.

In fact he's in the majority, with 6ft 7in Dan Burn one of the few team-mates to wear old school shin guards or 'cricket pads', as he's called them.

Burn does not lack for shin. Peter Crouch was another with proportions from the Cretaceous period to choose a bulkier protector but most current forwards, wingers in particular, favour the barely-there pads and those of a certain generation wince at the sight.

Matias Fernandez-Pardo shows his tiny shin pads (left) - The modern trend is in stark contrast to Peter Crouch's heavy duty option when he played (right)

What's the point 😂😂😂😂😂 pic.twitter.com/dA6dacRncw

For most who have played the game at an amateur standard, those medieval battle-ready Sondico shin pads with ankle protectors were the norm.

When the village meathead with the turning circle of Pavarotti is making it his mission to fill the local A&E department on a Sunday, that makes sense.

Brave? Stupid? Complacent? Or all in the aid of performance? Plenty of the criticism of modern pros centres on the supposedly heightened risk of a horrific injury.

The number of broken legs in the Premier League has declined over the past 15 years. Eduardo, Aaron Ramsey, Hatem Ben Arfa and Bobby Zamora all suffered agonising lower-leg fractures between 2006-2010.

Crucially, the officiating since then has evolved. Two-footed lunges, studs-up challenges and sliding in from behind will get you sent off and even if the referee doesn't pull the trigger, VAR is primed to jump in.

Leg breaks, from a direct impact on the shin at least, are a rarity now and damage is more likely to be cosmetic. Players are happy to risk cuts and scrapes to avoid wearing cumbersome pads that they feel are limiting.

Top orthopedic sport surgeon, Dr David Abbasi, who runs his own clinic Prime Ortho Center and works cageside for UFC fights, told the Daily Mail: 'The problem with miniature shin pads is that they leave a significant portion of the leg’s tibia bone exposed to direct impact.

'Properly sized firmer shin pads provide greater coverage and help absorb forces from kicks, reducing the risk of painful bone contusions, lacerations and potentially fractures.

'From an orthopedic standpoint, smaller pads compromise protection for comfort. For youth players with less kick accuracy, I would definitely recommend the regular shin pads.'

The miniature ones are perfectly legal. The official rule (4.2) gives plenty of wiggle room - failing to specify a certain size, shape or material shin pads have to conform to. And referees are only obliged to check that 'something' is being worn.

Even that low-level of scrutiny can be tricky for officials, with Hull's Sorba Thomas seen on Sky Sports last weekend  trying to convince the fourth official he was wearing protection.

He gestured to his low-cut socks, incredulously pointing at an outline akin to a communion wafer.

"They're almost like sim card size!" Sorba Thomas was held back from coming on for an issue with his socks! pic.twitter.com/kqR6wXnK0b

Tackles like this one from James Tarkowski on Yehor Yarmolyuk, for which he received a red card, are more severely punished now

Phi Foden is one of many players to have personalised shin pads worn in sock sleeves

Increasingly, the safety element has taken a backseat to aesthetic. Shin pads have become customised, monetised and personalised.

If the traditionalists were annoyed before, wait until Chloe Kelly shows them the dog photo on hers.

Aston Villa and Germany midfielder Leon Goretzka chose a topless picture of himself, flexing with the Champions League trophy during his Bayern Munich days.

Phil Foden has a cartoon impression of a family photo, while others have sponsors, religious iconography or inspirational messages written on theirs.

Some players have even pulled them out as a prop for goal celebrations.

Shin pads have been around since 1874, when Sam Weller Widdowson cut down his cricket pads and stuck them down his socks while playing for Nottingham Forest.

It quickly caught on but 152 years later, form is beating function.

Top players viewing shin pads with a lofty level of disdain rather than useful safeguard can have dangerous consequences for young, impressionable players who want to mirror their heroes.

David Platt holds up his shin pad alongside Gary Lineker after England beat Cameroon in 1990

Leon Goretzka (left) had a picture of himself topless on his own shin pads while on Germany duty

Two years ago, a 15-year-old turning out for Penistone Church, a team from Barnsley in South Yorkshire, suffered a gruesome double leg break while wearing tiny 3cm by 9cm shin pads.

He broke his tibular and fibula and later told the BBC: 'It’s not worth the extra bit of speed to have you knocked out of football for months and months. It’s not worth the risk.

'They were the most pathetic shin pads you've ever seen. Take a step back and look at the potential consequences of wearing them, and think, are they really worth it?'

Alfie broke his leg in what the club described as a fair 50/50 duel with no malicious intent from the opponent.

Top footballers playing in high stakes, strictly regulated games on the best surfaces with sports science behind them are clearly less exposed to risk than Sunday league players.

Also, the need for marginal gains is so much greater as players and teams seek any conceivable edge to performance in the professional game.

Trends inevitably filter downwards and grassroots players could heed the warning of Virgil van Dijk, one of the last of the dwindling 'proper' shin pad brigade.

'If you get kicked on your shin and your shin pad is that size of an AirPod, then obviously that's a big problem', the Liverpool skipper warned.

Virgil van Dijk is one of the few players who still wear larger protective shin pads

Luka Modric kisses the image of his children on his shin pad before coming on

The science tends to back him up. A 2018 peer-reviewed study by the National Library of Medicine retrieved data over 25 years in Dutch hospital A&E departments, before and after the law to wear shin pads at all levels was brought in.

They found: 'The incidence of lower leg football injuries decreased significantly following the introduction of the shin guard law (1996-2000: -20%; 2001-2005: -25%), whereas the incidence of all other football injuries did not.'

But the severity of those injuries varies and there's dubious evidence that shin pads are effective at stopping broken legs.

The bone tends to snap when studs are planted in the turf, rather than through a massive direct impact.

Whether players reach for the carbon fiber or custard cream option is ultimately a personal decision. But those who hobble their way to the hospital waiting room having chosen the latter might find sympathy in short supply.

#1152. Real Madrid tie Tchouaméni and Güler to 2032 contracts within 24 hours

Real Madrid have extended the contracts of Aurélien Tchouaméni and Arda Güler until June 2032, a day apart. With captain Fede Valverde also reportedly agreeing new terms, the club are securing their core midfield for years to come.

Real Madrid have committed two midfield regulars to long-term deals in the space of 24 hours. Güler’s announcement came first, and Aurélien Tchouaméni’s followed.

Both players are part of the core of Mourinho’s midfield. The renewals keep them at the club for six more seasons.

Tchouaméni arrived in 2022 and has made 205 appearances for the club. He has won eight trophies in that time. They include one Champions League, two Club World Cups and two UEFA Super Cups. He has also lifted one LaLiga, one Copa del Rey and one Spanish Super Cup.

His standing goes beyond the club. He has 50 France caps and won the 2021 Nations League. The new contract is worth around €9 million net per season, GOAL reported. The agreement came after interest from Manchester United.

Güler’s record covers a shorter spell. He was 18 when he joined. He has 38 caps for Turkey. In September he was named Breakthrough Player of the 2025-26 Champions League. His new salary is reportedly about €8m a year.

The two profiles differ. Tchouaméni is an established international with a full set of club honours. Güler is a younger player whose contract now runs almost nine years from his arrival. Tying both to the same end date suggests a midfield the club intend to keep together.

The club may not be finished. Captain Fede Valverde has agreed to extend his contract from 2029 to 2031, according to GOAL. The new deal will make him one of the squad’s highest earners. An announcement is expected soon, as Madrid work on further renewals after Güler and Tchouaméni.

If Valverde’s extension is confirmed, none of the three midfielders would have a contract ending before 2031. That would remove contract questions over a key part of the squad for several seasons. The two completed renewals arrived during the build-up to a busy run of home matches.

🚨🤍 Aurelien Tchouameni has signed new long term deal at Real Madrid until June 2032. pic.twitter.com/13BtcLyubP

— Fabrizio Romano (@FabrizioRomano) November 19, 2026

Tchouaméni has not been fully clear of fitness concerns this month. Earlier in November he left the France squad with a muscle problem. He was back in training with the Madrid squad on the day his renewal was announced.

Real Madrid host Celta at the Santiago Bernabéu on Saturday 21 November at 21:00 in LaLiga matchday 13. PSV then visit for a Champions League game on Tuesday 24 November.

#1151. Roberto Fernández goal earns Eder Sarabia’s Espanyol win at San Mamés

Espanyol beat Athletic Club 1-0 in Bilbao through a Roberto Fernández goal. The result extends a strong run since Manolo González left and leaves Athletic seventh after a home defeat in which they dominated the statistics.

A crowd of 46,107 was at San Mamés on Friday 20 November 2026. The fixture opened Matchday 13 of LaLiga EA Sports.

The win was Eder Sarabia’s second in charge of Espanyol and his second in a row away from home. The club have now taken seven of the nine points available since González left, according to EFE. Espanyol named Sarabia head coach on 28 October 2026, on a contract that runs until 2028.

His appointment followed a 4-3 Copa del Rey defeat at Sestao River. A 1-0 win at Villarreal, a 0-0 draw with Deportivo La Coruna and Friday’s victory in Bilbao make up Espanyol’s results since González’s exit. Their goal difference now stands at zero.

The first half ended goalless. Tyrhys Dolan replaced Pere Milla in the 57th minute. Sarabia also sent on Gabriel Moscardó and Javi Hernández in the 65th minute.

A minute later, Dolan set up Fernández for the winner. It was the striker’s sixth league goal of the season, putting him eighth in the LaLiga scoring list. He finished with 3 shots and a rating of 7.92.

Sarabia then brought on Unai Núñez and Javi Puado in the 84th minute to protect the lead. Clemens Riedel was booked in the third minute of stoppage time, Espanyol’s only card of the night.

Goalkeeper Ángel Fortuño made six saves to keep a clean sheet.

The result gave Espanyol a third successive league win over Athletic. They won 2-0 at home on 13 May 2026 and 2-1 at San Mamés on 22 December 2025.

Athletic controlled most of the statistics. They had 58% of possession and 9 corners to Espanyol’s 2. On target, the hosts had 6 efforts and the visitors 3.

Edin Terzić moved away from the 4-4-2 he had used in previous matches to fit Oihan Sancet into a 4-2-3-1. The change did not produce more attacking threat. Deia judged this to be Athletic’s worst performance at San Mamés since Terzić took charge.

Nico Williams had 5 shots and 3 key passes. Iñigo Ruiz de Galarreta also created 3 chances in 29 minutes on the pitch. Athletic collected three yellow cards, for Iñaki Williams, Ruiz de Galarreta and Yeray Álvarez.

Athletic fall to defeat at San Mames.#AthleticEspanyol #AthleticClub 🦁 pic.twitter.com/tRnTpjuX14

— Athletic Club (@Athletic_en) November 20, 2026

Before kick-off, San Mamés paid tribute to Elene Gurtubay and Daniela Agote, who won the Under-20 World Cup.

After 12 matches, Terzić’s side have 16 points. Their recent run reads one draw, two wins and one defeat in the league before Friday’s loss. Real Sociedad sit fifth on 22 points.

Athletic travel to bottom side Malaga on Saturday 28 November. Espanyol host Getafe on Monday 30 November.

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from today’s three Serie A games on the Liveblog.

“We have three healthy strikers at our disposal right now, Pio and Marcus have done really well in Lauti’s absence, but there are so many games and with only three forwards, we’ve got to rotate. It will be a different choice on Tuesday, and another different one next Saturday.”

Lazio are refusing to stall their momentum, so the pressure is already on Inter to keep up with the Serie A leaders.

#1149. Espí’s late winner seals ninth straight win as Real Madrid draw level with Barcelona

Substitute Carlos Espí struck late as Real Madrid came from behind to beat Celta Vigo 2-1 at the Santiago Bernabéu. The result keeps Madrid firmly in the title race with Barcelona.

The victory over Celta on Saturday 21 November 2026 was Madrid’s ninth in a row. It also kept their 100% home record this season intact.

The winner began with a Vinícius Júnior cross. Espí headed it, Celta goalkeeper Ionuț Radu saved, and the striker scored from the rebound in the six-yard box. He had been on the pitch for only a few minutes.

Espí had played only 44 minutes of LaLiga football this season before kick-off, according to ESPN. All three of his league goals have now won games, against Espanyol, Elche and Celta. He also scored in the 4-3 Champions League comeback win at Roma. The goal was his fourth of the season, the club said.

Espí called his first goal in front of the Bernabéu crowd his most special for the club. José Mourinho described him as a pure penalty-box striker. The coach added that football history has many players like him who decide games without playing many minutes.

Pablo Durán gave Celta a sixth-minute lead from a Williot Swedberg pass. Kylian Mbappé then missed a penalty in the 39th minute, and the visitors led 1-0 at the break.

Mourinho had started Vinícius and Federico Valverde on the bench. He sent them on with Marc Cucurella in the second half to chase the game. Thibaut Courtois kept Madrid in it with a strong low save from a long-range Durán shot in the 65th minute. A minute later, Jude Bellingham equalised from an Mbappé assist.

The figures show how one-sided the contest was. Madrid had 24 shots to Celta’s 8 and an expected goals total of 3.8 against 1.52. Radu made five saves, and the hosts held 64% of possession.

Celta coach Claudio Giráldez said Madrid’s substitutes had decided the game. He pointed out that he had started six academy graduates. Many of his players were appearing at the Bernabéu for the first time. Giráldez replaced Hugo Álvarez with Ferran Jutglà at half-time and sent on Iago Aspas for Durán in the 76th minute. Celta are 13th on 13 points.

Barcelona still top the table on goal difference, 35 to 22. They can move clear again when they host Villarreal on Sunday 22 November.

In the LaLiga scoring chart, Mbappé is second with 13 goals. Barcelona’s Raphinha leads on 15.

📞 Just call Carlos Espí. #LaLigaHighlights pic.twitter.com/z9KqjfkhmY

— Real Madrid C.F. 🇬🇧🇺🇸 (@realmadriden) November 21, 2026

Earlier on Saturday, Rafael Nadal was elected to Real Madrid’s board of directors at an Extraordinary General Assembly at Ciudad Real Madrid. Later, he watched the game from the stands and was visibly emotional.

Celta host Bournemouth in the Europa League at Balaídos on Thursday 26 November, with 3 points from four games. Madrid face PSV in the Champions League at the Bernabéu on Tuesday 24 November at 20:00 UTC. They have won all four of their league-phase games and sit second on 12 points, while PSV are 24th on 4 points.

#1147. Remarkable moment ashamed Southampton boss Tonda Eckert removes a box of tissues from his press conference: Manager left furious at his own club for lack of 'class' in bitter win over Spygate rivals Middlesbrough

Published: 16:57 EST, 27 November 2026 | Updated: 07:09 EST, 28 November 2026

Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert has insisted taunts aimed at Middlesbrough 'don't come from me' after the Championship club targeted their rivals in their first meeting since the Spygate saga.

The club conducted themselves disgracefully in a bitter reunion six months on from their ejection from last season’s play-off final.

Daily Mail Sport asked Eckert about a series of provocative gestures around the fixture and whether he needed to remind the club to keep it classy ahead of future matches with Middlesbrough.

A mortified Eckert removed a box of tissues from the press conference podium when they were highlighted by Daily Mail Sport.

The tissues were an apparent reference to Middlesbrough boss Kim Hellberg crying in his press conference at Southampton last season when Boro lost in the play-offs semi-final before being reinstated.

‘I hope everyone who came here from the Middlesbrough staff knows that these things don't come from me,' Eckert said after removing the box of tissues, having stared at them for 20 seconds.

#SaintsFC boss Tonda Eckert removes a box of tissues from the desk during his post-match press conference 🤧After their 2-0 win over leaders Middlesbrough, Eckert insists he just wants to focus on the football ⚽️Get more recation on BBC sounds 😇👇https://t.co/StIk7i3ZGg pic.twitter.com/eo6BRETKeW

Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert has insisted taunts aimed at Middlesbrough 'don't come from me' after the Championship club targeted their rivals over the Spygate saga

Hellberg cried in his press conference at Southampton last season and a box of tissues were shamelessly added  to the podium in the press conference room after Friday's match

‘Everything you do in defeat and if you win you do in class and I try to do that. I hope that there's an appreciation that this doesn't come from me.’

Saints beat Middlesbrough in last season’s play-off semi-final but were booted out by the EFL four days before the final after Daily Mail Sport revealed Southampton had sent their very own Johnny English to spy on Boro’s training sessions.

Both managers called for an armistice before the match but that memo clearly hadn't reached the Southampton marketing team, who posted an inflammatory video on social media.

The uncouth 79-second film mocked Boro, with the narrator declaring, ‘they got another go, their story continued’ over footage of Oli McBurnie’s winning goal for Hull City in the play-off final was also projected onto the big screen just eight minutes before kick-off.

'I didn't like the video this morning,’ Eckert said. If we look back a couple of months, the reality is both clubs have lost.

‘One club has lost off the pitch, and the other club has lost on the pitch. It’s an episode that is good to close for both clubs to move forward.

‘It’s time to move on at one point. For me, that episode from last year is closed. I've apologised. I've apologised to Kim (Hellberg). I've invited him for a drink. I just hope that we can do everything we do with class.'

Southampton won their first meeting since the Spygate scandal by earning a 2-0 win over their rivals, which included an on-pitch flare up between the sides.

Even Tonda Eckert is genuinely fed up of Southampton Football Club. pic.twitter.com/NjKZyQvDTi

Southampton's Finn Azaz mocked Middlesbrough's fans by pretending to cry after scoring

His celebration - in their first meeting since last season's 'Spygate' - sparked a brawl, with Azaz being booked

Southampton's Ryan Manning was seen celebrating their second goal with a pair of binoculars

Manning appeared to have picked up binoculars that had been thrown onto the pitch

Ryan Manning tucked James Bree’s cutback past Radek Vitek on 59 minutes to open the scoring for Saints before attacker Finn Azaz brought the contest to boiling point.

The former Boro forward scored Southampton’s second goal late on and then ran the length of the pitch to goad the away supporters by pretending to cry.

It sparked a fracas as Azaz and Will Lankshear – who wasn’t even at Boro last season when tensions were at their highest between the clubs – squared up, while travelling fans tried to get over the barricade.

Speaking after the match, Azaz said: 'They sang about me home and away last season, so I was just waiting for my moment to get one back. I have no regrets whatsoever.'

Manning was also pictured celebrating Southampton's second goal by looking through a pair of binoculars that appeared to have been thrown onto the pitch.

Binoculars had been handed out to Middlesbrough supporters prior to the match.

In a bitter reunion, Manning tucked James Bree’s neat cutback past Radek Vitek on 58 minutes before Azaz added a second as Southampton remained unbeaten at home in ten months. Saints, though, were needlessly provocative throughout.

The scenes calmed post-match but Southampton’s off-field operation humiliated the club – taking their celebration too far.

Binoculars had been handed out to Middlesbrough fans prior to the match at St Mary's

The Spygate saga was referenced by fans of both clubs around Friday night's clash

Southampton also reminded Hellberg of his tears following their play-off by playing Oasis' Stop Crying Your Heart Out over the speakers. Throughout the match, the Saints fans sang: 'We saw you cry on the telly.'

Hellberg added: 'In general, those who show more emotions and stand up for what is right are brave people. Hiding behind people and being afraid of emotions, that's the problem we have in the world a little bit.

'We have to hide from everything, how people are feeling, mental health and everything. It’s important we stand up for that – I'm not afraid of showing feelings.'

Considering Southampton started this season on minus four points for the breaches, their supporters’ staggering endorsement of the cheating was as indiscreet as the espionage itself.

‘We’ll spy when we want,’ sang the Southampton fans – a reminder of when their spy kid tried to conceal himself behind a tree near Middlesbrough’s training ground to film their training session. The EFL discovered three further spying missions on investigation.

Southampton fully embraced their cheats tag as they claimed three points, responding to chants of ‘you cheating b*******, you know what you are’ with sarcastic applause.

Victory moves Saints within four points of Middlesbrough, who remain top of the table going into the weekend but could slip down as far as fifth. Sadly, that was overshadowed by their crass conduct.

#1145. Suzuki howler costs Aston Villa crucial points

Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki went from being serenaded with a chorus of “world’s No 1” to making a bizarre blunder that denied Unai Emery’s side a third successive Premier League victory.

The Villa manager, however, preferred to focus on a string of important saves from Suzuki rather than the uncharacteristic mistake that allowed Fulham to collect a deserved point.

It all went wrong for the hosts just after the hour mark in a match where Fulham provided more than a few scares before finding the net in unexpected fashion.

Alex Iwobi, who had been denied superbly by a Suzuki save just moments earlier, swung in a corner. It was right on top of the Villa goalkeeper, who tried to keep it out but only succeeded in fumbling it over the line. A frantic attempt to gather the ball was in vain and goal-line technology confirmed the goal stood.

Zion Suzuki drops Alex Iwobi's corner and Fulham are level! 🫨 https://t.co/KwLFMRpKqk

Suzuki appeared to have been put off by the presence of Fulham’s Shea Charles, but Emery refused to single out the player for criticism.

“I prefer to speak about the saves that he made,” the Villa manager said. “This is part of football. I think he played fantastically and he is doing a lot of saves so he can make one mistake. It is part of football. We can be mature about this.

“I still want to see consistency. Over the last five Premier League matches, we are winning three and drawing two. It’s not bad but with our poor start it’s not enough.

“We have to change our mind quickly for Tuesday against Barcelona. We want to test ourselves at this level.”

Villa go to the Nou Camp with a 100 per cent Champions League record to their name this season. But they will need to improve on Saturday evening’s performance to get a result in Spain.

As well as Suzuki’s error, a 14th-minute penalty miss from John McGinn also proved costly.

It was awarded after Leon Goretzka, making his full league debut for Villa, saw his header hit Sander Berge’s raised hand. Nobody appealed at the time but referee Sam Barrott was sent to the touchline monitor by VAR to review the incident and gave the spot-kick.

McGinn’s attempt, however, hit the crossbar and the chance to take an early lead went begging. The Villa captain seemed a strange choice to take the spot-kick as he has only ever scored one career penalty, but Emery defended the choice, saying: “We analysed the penalty takers in the squad and it was McGinn here.”

Penalty MISSED! John McGinn hits the bar 💥 https://t.co/2kBYkYA2BY

Nicolas Jackson was on hand to ease Villa’s nerves before the break, though. the Villa manager had said before the game that the striker’s goalscoring capability meant he was capable of matching the likes of Harry Kane. His assessment was backed up by Jackson scoring the opening goal, after 40 minutes, which summed up the striker in one moment of pure power combined with agility.

Collecting Johan Manzambi’s superbly weighted pass, Jackson forced his way past two defenders before sliding in the goal that put Villa ahead.

Emery’s touchline celebrations said it all as the Senegal forward continues to flourish under the man who knew how to get the best out of him at Villarreal.

Nicolas Jackson scores his fifth league goal in five games! 🔥 https://t.co/W0xmFtW1Gt

Suzuki has also flourished under Emery and he kept Villa in the game with some superb saves.

When Antonee Robinson crossed for Gonzalo Garcia, his step over allowed Oscar Bobb in for what looked like his second goal in successive games. But Suzuki pulled off a stunning fingertip save. That had Villa supporters singing: “Zion Suzuki, the world’s No 1”.

Robinson put in another cross and Suzuki got a touch that was enough to make Garcia put his shot wide. Villa were living dangerously and the Japanese goalkeeper made another outstanding stop to keep out Iwobi’s header. But then it all went wrong for Suzuki when he fumbled Iwobi’s corner.

That allowed Fulham’s recent revival under manager, Alvaro Arbeloa, to continue – they now have seven points from their past three games.

“We spoke at half-time about what we had to do,” Arbeloa said. “If you want to win a game you have to fight and I think we have to believe in our way, we’ve shown we can beat anyone in the way that we play but we have to be aggressive.

“We created so many chances and at the end it’s one point in a difficult stadium. I’m so happy with the second half because of the way we played, this is the team that we want to be.”

"I don't think he gets the flowers he deserves" 💐 Jamie Redknapp is a fan of Calvin Bassey 🫡 https://t.co/R9uravAzRU

“We started the game well. Fulham are a good side, not easy to win [against] but we came in front. We did well but in the second half we gave them more time on the ball. They have good players and they can make chances. We were unlucky with the goal but we tried to keep fighting. It is important not to lose these games.”

On Zion Suzuki’s mistake for Fulham’s equaliser:

“It is frustrating because we do not want to concede goals but it can happen to everyone. Zion is a great guy, great goalkeeper. He will learn from it. We will support him and go again.”

The final whistle is blown at Villa Park and both sides take a point from the game. Aston Villa took the lead through Jackson but Suzuki’s blunder gifted Fulham the equalising goal. Fulham were fully deserving of a point this evening despite falling behind.

It’s half time at Villa Park and Unai Emery’s side are 1-0 ahead thanks to that man Nicolas Jackson’s eighth goal of the season. But Villa needed Japan goalkeeper Zion Suzuki to be on top form yet again.

Fulham almost took the lead when Antonee Robinson broke clear and crossed for Gonzalo Garcia, his step over allowed Oscar Bobb in for what looked like his second goal in successive games.

But Suzuki pulled off another stunning fingertip save following his impressive display against Manchester City last week. Cue a chorus of ‘Zion Suzuki, the world’s No1’ from the Holte End. Wait, wasn’t that Emi Martinez’s song last season?

Bassey is into the book late on in the half for a foul on Kamara.

King has a chance to equalise for Fulham but Suzuki is quick off his line to snuff out the danger. That is two big moments from Suzuki to prevent Fulham from scoring.

There will be four added minutes at the end of this first half.
